title: Basic Command-Line Argument Extraction
code:
import sys

# Simulated execution: python greet.py Arun Chennai
fake_argv = ['greet.py', 'Arun', 'Chennai']

script = fake_argv[0]
name = fake_argv[1]
city = fake_argv[2]

print('Script Name : %s' % script)
print('Name        : %s' % name)
print('City        : %s' % city)
explanation: Demonstrates the indexing anatomy of sys.argv where index 0 is the script and indices 1..n contain user parameters.

title: Validating Argument Count with len(sys.argv)
code:
import sys

# Safely handling missing CLI arguments
def run_cli(args):
    if len(args) < 3:
        print('Usage: python student.py <name> <age>')
        return
    name = args[1]
    age = int(args[2])
    print('Student %s is %d years old' % (name, age))

print('Test with missing arguments:')
run_cli(['student.py'])

print('\nTest with correct arguments:')
run_cli(['student.py', 'Arun', '20'])
explanation: Shows how checking len(sys.argv) prevents unhandled IndexError crashes when arguments are omitted.

title: Processing Dynamic Lists of Numbers with sys.argv[1:]
code:
import sys

# Simulated: python sum.py 10 20 30 40
simulated_argv = ['sum.py', '10', '20', '30', '40']

raw_nums = simulated_argv[1:]
numbers = [int(x) for x in raw_nums]
total = sum(numbers)
avg = total / len(numbers)

print('Parsed Numbers :', numbers)
print('Sum            : %d' % total)
print('Average        : %.2f' % avg)
explanation: Illustrates slicing sys.argv[1:] to process arbitrarily long lists of numbers passed from the command line.
